title: Generate Parentheses
description:
Given an integer `n`, produce every string made of exactly `n` opening and `n` closing parentheses that is **well-formed**: reading left to right, the number of `)` seen never exceeds the number of `(`, and the totals match at the end.

Return the strings in any order.

examples.explanation: There are 5 well-formed strings of length 6 (the third Catalan number).

hints: Build the string one character at a time. When is it still possible to add '(' ? When is it legal to add ')' ?
Track how many opens and closes you have used. Add '(' if open < n; add ')' if close < open.
Record the string when its length reaches 2n. Those two rules alone guarantee every produced string is balanced, so there is nothing to validate at the end.
approach:
**Key insight: a prefix can be extended to a balanced string iff it has used at most n opens and no more closes than opens.** Enforcing those two rules while building means the search never generates an invalid string, so the recursion tree has exactly as many leaves as answers.

**Algorithm.** `backtrack(open, close)`: record when the path has length `2n`. Otherwise, if `open < n` push `(` and recurse; if `close < open` push `)` and recurse; pop after each.

**Why it works.** The conditions are exactly the characterisation of prefixes of Dyck words. Every balanced string of length 2n has all its prefixes valid, so it is reached; every leaf has `open == close == n` and no bad prefix, so it is balanced.

**Common mistakes:** generating all 2^(2n) strings and filtering (exponentially slower); using `close < n` instead of `close < open`; string concatenation in the recursion is acceptable here but the list-plus-join form is cleaner to reason about.

**Interview follow-ups:** How many results are there? (the Catalan number C(n) = (2n)! / ((n+1)! n!).) A non-recursive construction? (closure form: every string is `(` A `)` B with A and B balanced of smaller sizes, which gives a DP over n.) Count only? (closed-form Catalan, or the DP in O(n^2).)

complexity.time: O(4^n / sqrt(n)) output-sensitive, i.e. proportional to the number of results times n
